title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Section (19) extends the earlier discussion of canonical metrics to conformal surfaces with boundary, possibly non-orientable. These are dianalytic surfaces, or Klein surfaces in modern terms.

(1) Grothendieck uses the standard equivalence of categories between conformal surfaces with boundary and Riemann surfaces without boundary equipped with an antiholomorphic involution σ.
- In one direction, X goes to its complex double X' (written X^or or X^σ). If X is orientable without boundary, X' = X ⊔ X̄, which matches the next page's example X = C, X' = C ⊔ C. If X is non-orientable without boundary, X' is the orientation double cover. If X has boundary, X' is the Schottky/Klein double.
- In the other direction, (X', σ) goes to the quotient X'/σ. The fixed locus of σ becomes the boundary of X.

(2) Definition: X is hyperbolic iff X' is hyperbolic. Since X' may be disconnected, this means each connected component of X' is hyperbolic.

(3) Consistency with the earlier definition. When X has no boundary, X' → X is an étale (unramified) double cover. So the universal covers agree componentwise, and the new definition coincides with the old one, which was in terms of the universal cover X̃.

(4) Compact or finite-type case.
- χ(X') = 2χ(X). Doubling along boundary circles adds nothing because circles have χ = 0, and étale double covers double χ.
- For finite-type Riemann surfaces, χ < 0 iff hyperbolic.
- Hence X is hyperbolic iff χ(X) < 0.
- For a holomorphic surface of type (g, ν), this reads 2g − 2 + ν ≥ 1, i.e. 2g + ν ≥ 3.

(5) He decides to keep the hyperbolicity hypothesis (on X, or possibly on Int X) in the 'conformation' (surgery) setting.

Purpose: the next page descends the canonical hyperbolic metric of X' to X. The boundary then becomes geodesic, because it is the fixed locus of an isometric involution. This sets up the surgery or gluing of conformal surfaces along geodesic boundaries, in the spirit of the pants-decomposition and Teichmüller-tower programme of the Esquisse.
errors: The closing remark says hyperbolicity 'is always true except if ν=0, g∈{0,1}'. By the criterion 2g+ν≥3 just derived, the exceptions are (g,ν) = (0,0), (0,1), (0,2) and (1,0): sphere, plane/disk, annulus/C*, torus. So (0,1) and (0,2) are omitted. Either this is a slip, or ν has a different meaning in this sentence.

'X compact ... de type (g,ν)' is loose. A surface with ν punctures is of finite type, not compact. The χ<0 criterion is nevertheless correct for finite-type surfaces, including bordered ones, via the double.

Minor: the χ formula and the hyperbolicity criterion are stated for connected X^or, but they also hold componentwise when X^or is disconnected (X orientable without boundary). The inserted note '(dans X^or connexe)' is thus unnecessary but harmless.

ideas.what: Equivalence between bordered, possibly non-orientable, conformal surfaces and Riemann surfaces with antiholomorphic involution, via the complex double
ideas.modern_name: Klein surfaces / dianalytic structures; complex (Schottky) double; real structures on Riemann surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Klein (1882), Schottky; formalized by Alling–Greenleaf (1971)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to surfaces with boundary and to the action of complex conjugation, but this explicit equivalence is not stated there as far as I know

ideas.what: Definition of hyperbolicity for a bordered surface via its double, and agreement with the universal-cover definition in the boundaryless case through étale covers

ideas.where_published: The condition 2g−2+ν>0 for M_{g,ν} appears in Esquisse d'un programme

deep.surprise_reason: The page is entirely classical: the Klein-surface/double equivalence, the hyperbolicity criterion via Euler characteristic, and (on the next page) descent of the metric with geodesic boundary. It is careful bookkeeping for the surgery project and contains a small slip in the exceptional cases. There is nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Title parenthetical: plausibly '(y compris non orientables)'. The handwriting is abbreviated but this reading fits the content.

The superscript in 'X' = X^{or}' is ambiguous in the image (it could read σ or 'or'). The next page's transcription uses X^σ for the same object. It denotes the complex double, which is the orientation cover only in the boundaryless non-orientable case.
'Mais on gardera dans la conformation cette condition, ou celle que I.X soit hyperbolique': the 'I.X' is plausibly 'Int X' (the interior of X) rather than 'i.e.'.
'P.ex. si X est holomorphe compacte' may instead read 'holomorphe o-connexe' (i.e. connected), which matches the notation 'o-connexe' on the previous page.
The marginal insertion reads approximately '(dans X^or connexe)' and is attached to 'Si X est compact, comme on a'.
